paragraphs.title: The Philistines Seek to Return the Ark

answers: Seven months
Five months
One year
easy.explanation: The ark was in the Philistines' country seven months.
easy.q: How long was the ark of the Lord in the country of the Philistines?

answers: The kings and soldiers
The priests and diviners
The people of Bethshemesh
easy.explanation: They called for the priests and diviners.
easy.q: Whom did the Philistines call for advice about the ark?

answers: Weapons
New garments
A trespass offering
easy.explanation: They were told not to send the ark empty, but to return a trespass offering.
easy.q: What were the Philistines told to send with the ark?

answers: To give glory to the God of Israel and seek relief from the plague
To prepare the ark for a long journey
To mark the border of Philistia
medium.explanation: The offering was meant to give glory to God and perhaps lighten His hand upon them.
medium.q: What was the purpose of the trespass offering?

answers: A place of residence
An offering made because of guilt or wrongdoing
A box used to carry the ark
medium.explanation: A trespass offering was given because of guilt or an offense.
medium.q: In the KJV, what does “trespass offering” mean in this context?

answers: To explain how to build a cart
To describe the land of Israel
To warn the Philistines not to harden their hearts
medium.explanation: They reminded the Philistines that Egypt and Pharaoh hardened their hearts but eventually let Israel go.
medium.q: Why did the priests and diviners mention Egypt and Pharaoh?

answers: The Philistines recognized that they had offended the God of Israel
The Philistines wanted to keep the ark
The ark was missing some of its parts
challenge.explanation: The offering showed recognition of their offense and a desire to honor the God of Israel.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the command to return the ark with an offering rather than empty-handed?

answers: The healing was only for the people of Bethshemesh
Returning the ark with an offering could show whether the plague would be removed
The ark itself was used as medicine
challenge.explanation: The priests said that the Philistines might be healed and know why the Lord's hand was not removed from them.
challenge.q: How was healing connected with returning the ark?

answers: Whether to fight or surrender
Whether to hide or sell the ark
Whether the plague came from the Lord or by chance
challenge.explanation: The following test was intended to distinguish the Lord's hand from a chance event.
challenge.q: What uncertainty is reflected in the words of the Philistines and their advisers?

short_answers.question: What did the priests and diviners tell the Philistines to do with the ark?
short_answers.answer: They told them to send it back with a trespass offering.
short_answers.explanation: They said not to send the ark away empty.

short_answers.question: What did the priests warn the Philistines not to do?
short_answers.answer: They warned them not to harden their hearts.
short_answers.explanation: They referred to the example of Egypt and Pharaoh.

short_answers.question: What might happen if the Philistines returned the ark with an offering?
short_answers.answer: They might be healed, and they would know why the Lord's hand had not been removed from them.
short_answers.explanation: This is the promise stated in the KJV text.

paragraphs.title: The Test of the Cart and the Cows

answers: A new cart
A large ship
A stone chest
easy.explanation: They were told to make a new cart.
easy.q: What did the Philistines prepare to carry the ark?

answers: Three
Two
Five
easy.explanation: They took two milch kine and tied them to the cart.
easy.q: How many milch kine were tied to the cart?

answers: Ekron
Ashdod
Bethshemesh
easy.explanation: The test directed them toward Bethshemesh.
easy.q: Where were the cows directed to go?

answers: They shut them up at home
They sent them ahead of the cart
They placed them on the cart
medium.explanation: Their calves were shut up at home.
medium.q: What did the Philistines do with the calves?

answers: If the cows returned to Ekron
If the cows went up the way to Bethshemesh
If the cart broke
medium.explanation: Going toward Bethshemesh would indicate that the Lord had caused the plague.
medium.q: What sign did the Philistines establish?

answers: The cows traveled very quickly
The cows stopped near the city
The cows did not leave the appointed road
medium.explanation: They went straight along the highway without turning aside.
medium.q: What does “turned not aside to the right hand or to the left” mean?

answers: The cows had a natural reason to return, so going to Bethshemesh was significant
It made the cart easier to pull
It protected the ark from thieves
challenge.explanation: The cows would naturally want to return to their calves, so their going away from them was a meaningful sign.
challenge.q: Why did keeping the calves at home strengthen the meaning of the test?

answers: That the cart was well made
That the plague came from the Lord and was not merely chance
That Bethshemesh was close to Ekron
challenge.explanation: Their unusual, purposeful behavior confirmed the Lord's intervention.
challenge.q: What did the cows' straight journey to Bethshemesh demonstrate to the Philistines?

answers: They forced the cows to move
They carried the calves
They followed the cows to the border of Bethshemesh
challenge.explanation: The lords of the Philistines went after the cows unto the border of Bethshemesh.
challenge.q: What did the lords of the Philistines do during the test?

short_answers.question: What was placed in the coffer beside the ark?
short_answers.answer: The golden jewels returned as a trespass offering, including the golden mice and images of the emerods.
short_answers.explanation: The offerings were placed in a coffer by the side of the ark.

short_answers.question: What did the cows do as they went toward Bethshemesh?
short_answers.answer: They took the straight way, went along the highway, and did not turn aside.
short_answers.explanation: The KJV says they went straight while lowing as they went.

short_answers.question: What did the Philistine lords do after sending the cart away?
short_answers.answer: They followed the cows unto the border of Bethshemesh.
short_answers.explanation: Their following allowed them to observe the result of the test.

answers: They rejoiced
They fled
They hid it
easy.explanation: They rejoiced to see the ark.
easy.q: What did the people of Bethshemesh do when they saw the ark?

answers: In the field of Joshua, a Bethshemite
In the country of the Philistines
At Kirjathjearim
easy.explanation: The cart came into the field of Joshua, a Bethshemite, and stood there.

answers: The golden jewels only
The cows as a burnt offering and sacrifices
The cart alone
easy.explanation: They offered the cows as a burnt offering and sacrificed sacrifices unto the Lord.
easy.q: What did the people of Bethshemesh offer unto the Lord?

answers: They returned them to the Philistines
They placed them on the great stone
They carried them into Joshua's house
medium.explanation: The Levites put the ark and the coffer on the great stone.
medium.q: What did the Levites do with the ark and the coffer?

answers: Sacrifices offered upon the altar
People going up to the city
Objects lifted onto a cart
medium.explanation: Burnt offerings were sacrifices presented to the Lord.
medium.q: What are “burnt offerings” in this passage?

answers: To identify the five rulers and their cities
To show that the gold came from Bethshemesh
To describe the route of the cart
medium.explanation: The offerings corresponded to the five lords and their cities.
medium.q: Why were the golden emerods listed according to Philistine cities?

answers: Their joy was joined with recognition of the Lord's honor
The cows belonged to the people of Bethshemesh
The Philistines remained in the city
challenge.explanation: The people rejoiced while also honoring the Lord through offerings and sacrifices.
challenge.q: What does the combination of rejoicing and sacrifice show about the people's response?

answers: It was the place where the ark and coffer were set
It was a wall against the Philistines
It marked the border of Ekron
challenge.explanation: The ark and the coffer were placed upon the great stone.
challenge.q: What was the role of the great stone in the return of the ark?

answers: They stayed to work in Bethshemesh
They observed the outcome and left the ark with Israel
They carried the ark onward to Kirjathjearim
challenge.explanation: After seeing what happened, the Philistine lords returned to Ekron, while the ark remained in Bethshemesh.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the Philistine lords returning to Ekron that same day?

short_answers.question: What were the people of Bethshemesh doing when they first saw the ark?
short_answers.answer: They were reaping their wheat harvest in the valley.
short_answers.explanation: The verse says they were reaping when they lifted up their eyes and saw the ark.

short_answers.question: Where did the cart stop?
short_answers.answer: It stopped in the field of Joshua, a Bethshemite, where there was a great stone.
short_answers.explanation: This was the place where the ark was removed from the cart.

short_answers.question: What did the five Philistine lords do after seeing the events?
short_answers.answer: They returned to Ekron the same day.
short_answers.explanation: The KJV explicitly records their return to Ekron.

paragraphs.title: The Blow at Bethshemesh and the Ark's Transfer

answers: They received the ark with joy only
They were smitten with a great slaughter
They went to fight the Philistines
easy.explanation: The Lord smote the men of Bethshemesh because they had looked into the ark.
easy.q: What happened to the men of Bethshemesh?

answers: The holy Lord God
The king of the Philistines
The God of Egypt
easy.explanation: They asked, “Who is able to stand before this holy Lord God?”
easy.q: How did the men of Bethshemesh describe the Lord?

answers: The lords of the Philistines
The inhabitants of Kirjathjearim
The priests of Egypt
easy.explanation: They sent messengers to the inhabitants of Kirjathjearim.
easy.q: To whom did the men of Bethshemesh send messengers?

answers: They lamented and recognized the holiness of the Lord
They carried the ark back to Ekron
They ignored what had happened
medium.explanation: The people lamented because the Lord had smitten many of them.
medium.q: What was the response of the people of Bethshemesh to the blow?

answers: They wanted to return it to the Philistines
They realized the holy ark should be received elsewhere
The cart had broken
medium.explanation: They asked who could stand before the holy Lord God and sought another place for the ark.
medium.q: Why did they seek to transfer the ark?

answers: Who can win a war?
Who can hold the cart?
Who can remain before the holiness of the Lord without judgment?
medium.explanation: The question expresses fear and recognition of the Lord's holiness.
medium.q: What does “Who is able to stand before this holy Lord God?” express?

answers: They moved from rejoicing at its return to recognizing the need for reverence
They moved from fear to indifference
They moved from wanting to return it to the Philistines to wanting to keep it
challenge.explanation: Their joy at seeing the ark was followed by fear and recognition of its holiness.
challenge.q: What change occurred in the people's attitude toward the ark?

answers: It caused the people to seek another place for the ark
It caused them to send gifts to the Philistines
It caused them to deny the ark's holiness
challenge.explanation: After the judgment, they asked the inhabitants of Kirjathjearim to fetch the ark.
challenge.q: How did the blow lead to the sending of messengers?

answers: They were seeking people who could receive and care for the ark
They wanted to carry the ark to the top of a mountain
They thought the ark belonged to the Philistine lords
challenge.explanation: Their question led them to send for the inhabitants of Kirjathjearim.
challenge.q: What is implied by the question, “To whom shall he go up from us?”

short_answers.question: Why were the men of Bethshemesh smitten?
short_answers.answer: They had looked into the ark of the Lord.
short_answers.explanation: The KJV states that the Lord smote them because they had looked into the ark.

short_answers.question: What question did the people ask after the judgment?
short_answers.answer: They asked, “Who is able to stand before this holy Lord God?”
short_answers.explanation: Their words expressed fear before the Lord's holiness.

short_answers.question: What request did they send to the inhabitants of Kirjathjearim?
short_answers.answer: They asked them to come down and fetch the ark up to them.
short_answers.explanation: The messengers announced that the Philistines had brought back the ark and asked them to receive it.
